sections.markdown:
## A — Light, weather and driving emergencies
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers light, weather and driving emergencies for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC13-EXAM, WY-SEC13-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC13-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## B — Light, weather and driving emergencies
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with light, weather and driving emergencies as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants study reduced light, weather and the handbook's conditional emergency responses; vehicle-specific operating sequences require the applicable manufacturer information.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

sections.domain: Light, weather and driving emergencies — C.01
sections.heading: C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Night driving combines reduced visibility, oncoming glare, crossing animals and eyestrain, requiring greater alertness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Headlights are required from one-half hour after sunset through one-half hour before sunrise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Headlights are also required when low light or adverse weather prevents clearly seeing people and vehicles 1,000 feet ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can identify the vehicle and its actions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Parking lights alone are not lawful when headlights are required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Increase following space when you cannot see clearly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
In the handbook's night-driving illustration, traveling above 55 mph exceeds the distance illuminated far enough ahead for a stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Use high beams on rural highways and low beams when following, meeting oncoming traffic or driving in town. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
Dim headlights at least 500 feet before meeting another vehicle; the handbook describes that as about four to five seconds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
When approaching within 300 feet behind another vehicle, dim headlights to the lowest beam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Low beams must be aimed to avoid glare at all times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
Clean both sides of the windshield to reduce glare from oncoming vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A02
Clean headlights improve the light available for seeing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Keep the eyes moving rather than staring at the headlight spot, which can contribute to eyestrain, fatigue and poor concentration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
At night, scan for animals, pedestrians and bicycles and look sideways for lights from vehicles entering or crossing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
Check the lights of vehicles ahead for signs of speed or lane-position changes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Use low-beam headlights in fog; front fog lights may sometimes help. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Use red rear fog lights only in heavy fog or similar hazardous weather that seriously reduces visibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
Switch rear fog lights off once visibility improves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Reduce normal speed in fog while watching the difference from surrounding traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
The fog discussion warns of high crash risk when speed differs from other traffic by more than 15 mph. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

sections.domain: Light, weather and driving emergencies — C.02
sections.heading: C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
Stop at the nearest safe location if fog could create a large speed difference from other traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
If fog prevents seeing at least 10 seconds ahead, consider pulling off at the nearest safe place and stopping. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
In poor visibility, scan for vehicle lights, pedestrians and stopped or slow vehicles while enlarging the space cushion as much as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Slow down on slippery pavement because stopping distance increases. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
In rain, double a car's following interval to four seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
Use low-beam headlights during rain. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
Replace wiper blades if they smear or streak the windshield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Use extra care during the first half hour of rain, when dust and oil mix with water and make the road slippery. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin water film rather than the pavement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A03
Slowing down helps prevent hydroplaning during rain. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A03
The snow-and-ice guidance recommends snow tires or chains to resist skidding and reduce stopping distance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A03
On snow or ice, avoid sudden speed or direction changes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A03
Watch for ice on bridges and shaded road areas. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A03
For snow, the source triples a car's forward cushion to six seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A03
For ice, the source quadruples a car's forward cushion to eight seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A03
Keep vehicle windows clear to see and communicate with other road users. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A03
On snow or ice, slow gradually and smoothly before stopping or turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F39 | anchor: A03
Avoid locking the wheels because steering control depends on their rotation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F40 | anchor: A03
Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F41 | anchor: A03
Wind is particularly hazardous for trucks, recreational vehicles, campers and trailer-towing drivers, and lower speed is the source's recommended defense. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0079]

Misconceptions: Pumping conventional brakes and holding steady ABS pressure are different instructions; emergency acceleration is discussed only for a side or rear threat when room exists.
Mnemonics: Recall index: condition, braking system, space, controlled response; this organizer adds no emergency maneuver to the source.
Glossary: Recall terms: low beam, rear fog light, hydroplaning, ABS, blowout, steering lock and shoulder.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle-specific procedures, equipment capabilities and present legal applicability remain edition-bound. No old ignition-system table is generalized to modern vehicles.

sections.domain: Light, weather and driving emergencies — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
After leaving a wind-protected area for open space, be ready to correct steering as wind changes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Meeting a large truck or bus can bring sudden wind changes requiring steering corrections. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Be especially alert to wind effects on wet or slippery surfaces. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
Avoid driving in a blizzard whenever possible and obtain local severe-weather information. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
If stranded or ditched during a blizzard, stay with the vehicle so rescuers can locate you more easily. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
While stranded in a blizzard, leave a window open slightly for fresh air. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
Run the engine and heater sparingly with an open window, and ensure snow is not blocking the exhaust pipe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A01
While stranded, move the arms and legs periodically rather than remaining in one position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A01
Use emergency flashers to make a stranded vehicle visible and switch on the dome light at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A01
When several people are stranded together, take turns watching rather than all sleeping at once. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A01
Avoid overexertion and overexposure while stranded in a blizzard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
For conventional braking in an imminent-crash response, pump the brakes to preserve control and steering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
Hard, unchanging pressure on conventional brakes can cause a skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
With anti-lock brakes, use hard, steady pedal pressure because the system adjusts automatically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A02
If collision cannot otherwise be avoided, turn away from a head-on impact, generally to the right and off the roadway if necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A02
The turn-away guidance advises avoiding braking during the evasive turn to reduce skid risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A02
For a collision threat from the side or rear, accelerate only if room exists, then slow again after the danger passes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A02
When an impact is unavoidable, favor a glancing collision over a head-on impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A02
If an object must be struck, the handbook favors something more likely to give way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A02
If the accelerator sticks, concentrate on steering and keep looking at the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A02
Try freeing a stuck accelerator with the foot; if unsuccessful, use the clutch or shift to neutral. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A02
For a stuck accelerator, brake to a stop at the nearest safe location and switch off the ignition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A02
Have the sticking-accelerator cause identified and repaired. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

sections.domain: Light, weather and driving emergencies — C2.02
sections.heading: C2 — Light, weather and driving emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Light, weather and driving emergencies
FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A02
In a skid, stay calm and avoid overreacting. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A02
In the conventional-brake skid procedure, ease off hard braking or excessive acceleration if that action started the skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A03
The source explicitly distinguishes its conventional-brake skid procedure from ABS procedures. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A03
During skid recovery, steer to keep the vehicle aligned with the road and avoid oversteering. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A03
As the skid ends, be ready to steer in the opposite direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A03
Consult the owner's manual for special front-wheel-drive skid instructions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A03
In an ABS emergency, press firmly, keep pressure on the pedal and steer out of danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A03
Know which braking system the vehicle has before applying its emergency procedure. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A03
The brake-failure procedure calls for a lower gear and finding an off-roadway place to slow and stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A03
When using a release-equipped parking brake during brake failure, hold the release so braking can be eased if the rear wheels lock and a skid begins. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A03
Do not continue driving to a garage after brake failure. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A03
After a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle traveling straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R36 | anchor: A03
For a blowout, ease off the accelerator without immediately applying the brakes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R37 | anchor: A03
Once control returns after a blowout, brake gently and pull off at the nearest safe location. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R38 | anchor: A03
Use caution when changing a tire after a blowout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R39 | anchor: A03
If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, slow and try to warn its driver with headlight flashes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R40 | anchor: A03
If the oncoming vehicle continues toward you, move as far right as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R41 | anchor: A03
If that vehicle still approaches and collision threatens, steer off the roadway to the right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec13-R42 | anchor: A04
With a steering-lock device, never turn the ignition key to LOCK while moving because steering can lock and control can be lost. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-R43 | anchor: A04
After running off the pavement, keep calm, hold the wheel firmly and prepare for sudden shocks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-R44 | anchor: A04
While recovering from leaving the pavement, remain on the shoulder and ease off the accelerator. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-R45 | anchor: A04
Brake gently and reduce speed gradually while on the shoulder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec13-R46 | anchor: A04
After slowing on the shoulder, check traffic behind and ahead before returning toward the roadway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0083]
